rationale: The assistant immediately delivered the required safety stop, correctly explaining that 'the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged', told the customer to refit the cover, held firm when challenged, and gave a well-calibrated view of the HV circuit (diode, capacitor, transformer, magnetron or inverter) rather than fixating on the magnetron, with appropriate engineer-or-replace escalation. It stayed faithful to the customer's evidence and invented nothing. Weaknesses are a verbatim repeated opening sentence and safety panel across both turns, and a confusing stray line ('A lower power/defrost or combination setting is the simpler alternative') that adds nothing; it also never asked for the model number or cost tolerance, though the conversation was short.
